text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a regression on SM90 / CUDA12 FlashAttention variant for short sequences (<=64). p50 tokens/sec down ~25% in the canary vs prod :eyes:

maria: Which model + workload? can you paste numbers?

alex: Small internal 2B chat model, endpoint `chat-small`. Baseline (prod, CUDA11.8, legacy-cuda kernel): p50 ~19.4k t/s. Canary (CUDA12.1, triton-flashx-sm90): p50 ~14.6k t/s. Latency P95 also up ~40ms.

devin: Do you have micro-profiles? sounds like KV or memcpy regression when seq is short and batching small.

alex: Yep, pulled a short nsys snapshot. Key lines:
```
KV memcpy (host->device): 0.92ms -> 2.71ms (baseline -> canary)
attention_kernel (triton_flashx): 0.61ms -> 0.55ms
batching overhead (scheduling): 0.10ms -> 0.45ms
Overall per-token cost up ~1.8x for short sequences
```

timo: So the attention kernel got slightly faster but the KV memcpy and scheduling dominate for short seq — that matches what we saw with the paged-kv changes. Is the KV layout different in the new kernel?

alex: Looks like the new kernel expects 256B-aligned KV blocks for SM90 vectorization; our runtime still packs at 128B for small batches, so we see extra copy+pad on the hot path. The copy path was recently optimized and appears to take a hit under CUDA12's async copy semantics.

maria: Is this Triton-specific or CUDA runtime behavior?

devin: My local repro: switching to the CUDA-native fused attention (legacy-cuda) eliminates the memcpy spike. So it's combination: Triton kernel relies on aligned KV views and our selector did an unaligned fastpath that now forces a fallback memcpy.

jen: Can we hotfix selector logic to prefer legacy-cuda for seq <= 64 on SM90 until we fix alignment? Might be the least risky.

alex: I prototyped a selector tweak — if avg_seq <= 64 AND device_arch >= sm90 then prefer `legacy-cuda` kernel. Quick bench: p50 back to 18.9k t/s, P95 down. Tradeoff: slightly worse perf for mid sequences where flashx is better.

benchbot: Ran 10k sample microbench after selector patch:
```
config: 8xA100-sm90, seq=32, batch=8
baseline(prod): p50 19.4k t/s, p95 210ms
canary (triton-flashx): p50 14.6k t/s, p95 260ms
selector-patch: p50 18.9k t/s, p95 215ms
```

timo: Sounds reasonable. We should also open a follow-up to fix KV layout/pad logic in the triton kernels so they don't rely on our runtime doing the extra copies.

devin: Also want to investigate CUDA12 memcpy async behavior — maybe we can use `cudaMemcpyAsync` with different stream priorities to hide the copy. I have a small patch to try coalesced device copies.

jen: Ops: we need a quick canary rollback config while we iterate. Deploy-bot, can you spin 5% traffic to `selector-patch`?

deploy-bot: routing update requested by @jen — canary 5% -> `selector-patch` route created. Monitoring hooks: latency & error budget enabled.

sre-bot: Alert rule temp: create perf-alert if p50 drop > 15% for 5m on endpoint `chat-small`.

alex: Filed issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-7234 (perf-regression, label: regression/perf). Assigning to @timo. Added logs and attached nsys capture.

timo: I'll own kernel follow-up, will look at triton kernel alignment and padding. Putting a TODO to test CUDA11.8 vs CUDA12.1 memcpy microbench with different alignment vectors.

jen: Great. Next steps: (1) keep selector-patch canary at 5% until noon PT, (2) devin/timo investigate kernel alignment and memcpy async, (3) if simple fix for Triton exists, submit draft PR and we can canary.

alex: Thanks — will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
